faq.q: What specific material properties make Titanium Compressor Casing Segment suitable for Compressor case aft section?
faq.a: Titanium Compressor Casing Segment uses Grade 5 Ti-6Al-4V because its yield strength, fatigue endurance, and corrosion resistance directly address engine component operational demands. The alloy's specific strength enables mass reduction without section compromise, while the TiO2 passivation ensures long-term environmental resistance.

faq.q: What are the critical dimensional tolerances for Titanium Compressor Casing Segment?
faq.a: Standard machining tolerance for Titanium Compressor Casing Segment is +/-0.05mm (ISO 2768-m). Functional mating surfaces are held to +/-0.025mm with Ra 0.8um finish, verified specifically for compressor case aft requirements. Threaded features conform to ISO 965-2 Class 6g, verified with calibrated Go/No-Go ring gauges on 100% of production.

faq.q: Does Titanium Compressor Casing Segment require any post-machining surface treatment?
faq.a: Yes. compressor case aft components require Shot peening Almen 0.008-0.012A inducing compressive residual stress for extended HCF life in aerospace service — tailored for compressor case aft application. This restores the natural TiO2 passive layer removed during machining and provides the required surface properties for the specific service environment. Key parameters include surface finish Ra 0.8um and passive layer thickness verification per applicable standards.
